text:
Tara S.: forwarding a BrightWare ticket — they're seeing streaming responses cut off before the final JSON is emitted. client gets a partial object, no finish_reason, connection just closes. happened a few times after an auth refresh. repro attached by customer.

Raj P.: can you paste the exact curl/headers they used? and any proxy in front of them?

Tara S.: customer curl: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate -d '{"model":"rw-large","input":"..."}'
```
They included the tail of the SSE stream:
```
data: {"token":"Hello "}
data: {"token":"world"}
data: {"token":"!"}
data: {"done":true}
```
Then connection closes. No terminal event with finish_reason, and client-side JSON parse fails. They say auth refresh kicked at ~52s.

Maria I.: curious — do they sit behind Fastly/Cloudflare or an internal gateway? That timing smells like an idle/keepalive or a midstream auth rotation.

Tara S.: internal API gateway with 60s idle timeout. They said their client does token rotate around 50–55s which triggers a reconnect. Customer also tried repro where the SDK refresh aborts the fetch mid-stream and reports truncated output.

Jun (SDK): I can reproduce with node-fetch + AbortController if you trigger a token refresh and call abort(). Node's fetch will close the socket and you can lose the final event bytes. Quick workaround: set keepalive: true and/or send periodic SSE comments from server (": keepalive\n\n") to prevent idle timeouts. Also ensure client doesn't call abort() during expected finalization.

Raj P.: can we check server-side whether the runtime wrote the final sentinel? any req id?

Tara S.: request id is req_0a1b2c, customer timestamped ~1717654319.

sre-bot: logs for req_0a1b2c show: worker wrote final event and attempted flush at 1717654320. TCP FIN followed by RST from client IP 3.4.5.6 at 1717654321.

Maria I.: that suggests the client/edge reset before the full flush completed. two possibilities: client abort or edge/proxy trimming trailing bytes when upstream closes. we do have a proxy flush buffer limit (16KB) — if the final payload size crosses a flush boundary and the client dies mid-flush you can lose the tail.

Raj P.: any quick mitigation we can push from server side?

Jun (SDK): short-term: SSE keepalives and ensure we write a small final marker early (dup the finish_reason in a prior chunk) so clients parsing incrementally can see finish_reason sooner. also advise clients to implement a small post-stream poll (GET /runs/:id/status) to confirm finalization.

Maria I.: ops action: add a 200ms linger-on-close before we fully relinquish socket on write-complete; also enable an explicit flush for final sentinel to try to push trailing bytes. I'll open a deploy ticket. Long-term: make the runtime confirm final write ACK from kernel-level socket writes.

Raj P.: product ask — is the customer billed if final token never reached client?

Tara S.: they reported being charged for the generation. Raj, can you confirm billing logic?

Raj P.: billing is based on tokens produced by the runtime, not strictly on client-side receipt. if the generation completed server-side we will count those tokens. but if the runtime aborted mid-generation due to client disconnect we should not bill. We need to cross-check generator-complete vs stream-complete metrics for req_0a1b2c.

Jun (SDK): for customers affected, share this SDK workaround and suggest they increase gateway idle timeout or send keepalives. also we can add a recommended pattern in docs: "if you rotate auth mid-stream, do graceful drain and poll final status".

Tara S.: action items: 1) ask BrightWare for a tcpdump/pcap on their side showing the RST, 2) provide SDK workaround + docs snippet, 3) ops: implement final flush + 200ms linger tweak and enable server keepalive comments, 4) billing: Raj to audit req_0a1b2c and refund if server aborted before generator finish.

Maria I.: I'll create infra ticket INF-1427 and target a small rollback-safe change to flush+linger in the next patch window.

Raj P.: I'll check billing logs and update here.

Tara S.: thanks all — I'll reply to the customer with interim guidance (keepalive/comments + avoid abort during token refresh) and request pcap. :thumbsup:
